summary.one_liner: Coverage.py is a Python code coverage tool that measures which lines of code are executed, typically during test runs.
summary.what_it_does: Measures code coverage for Python programs, usually while the test suite runs. It uses the code analysis and tracing hooks in the Python standard library to determine which lines are executable and which have actually been executed. The README states it supports Python 3.11 through 3.16.0a1, including free-threading, and PyPy3 version 3.11. Full documentation is hosted on Read the Docs, with a Quick Start section for running coverage on a test suite. Code and the issue tracker are on GitHub.
use_cases: measure test coverage of a Python project
run coverage on a pytest or unittest suite
generate coverage reports for CI pipelines
check which code paths tests exercise
how_to_run: See the Quick Start section of the documentation on Read the Docs
notable: Uses the standard library's code analysis and tracing hooks rather than external instrumentation
Documentation hosted on Read the Docs with a change history page
caveats: Enterprise support is offered through a Tidelift subscription
README lists supported versions only as Python 3.11 onward and PyPy3 3.11; older Python versions are not covered
